title: The wrong medicine
setting: Saturday afternoon at the flat Sora shares with Kenta. Kenta has told Mai that Sora is ill in bed, so she drops by to check on him.

speakers.name: Mai
speakers.voice: female, late 20s, warm, a little shy

lines.speaker: mai
lines.romaji: sora, daijoubu? kenta kara kiita yo. netsu ga aru n da tte?
lines.ja: ソラ、大丈夫？ケンタから聞いたよ。熱があるんだって？
lines.kana: そら、だいじょうぶ？けんたからきいたよ。ねつがあるんだって？
lines.english: Sora, are you OK? Kenta told me. You've got a fever?

lines.speaker: sora
lines.romaji: un. kinou kara. nodo mo itai shi, saiaku da yo.
lines.ja: うん。昨日から。喉も痛いし、最悪だよ。
lines.kana: うん。きのうから。のどもいたいし、さいあくだよ。
lines.english: Yeah, since yesterday. My throat hurts too. It's awful.

lines.speaker: mai
lines.english: What about the doctor? Have you been?

lines.speaker: sora
lines.romaji: byouin wa ittenai. demo, kusuri nonderu kara daijoubu.
lines.ja: 病院は行ってない。でも、薬飲んでるから大丈夫。
lines.kana: びょういんはいってない。でも、くすりのんでるからだいじょうぶ。
lines.english: No, I haven't. But I'm taking medicine, so I'm fine.

lines.speaker: mai
lines.romaji: sou na n da. de, kusuri wa kiita?
lines.ja: そうなんだ。で、薬は効いた？
lines.kana: そうなんだ。で、くすりはきいた？
lines.english: I see. So, has the medicine helped?

lines.speaker: sora
lines.romaji: uun, zenzen kikanai n da yo. kono kusuri, kinou kara nonderu noni.
lines.ja: ううん、全然効かないんだよ。この薬、昨日から飲んでるのに。
lines.kana: ううん、ぜんぜんきかないんだよ。このくすり、きのうからのんでるのに。
lines.english: Nope, it's not doing a thing. And I've been taking it since yesterday.

lines.speaker: mai
lines.romaji: chotto misete. e, kore, onaka no kusuri da yo!
lines.ja: ちょっと見せて。え、これ、お腹の薬だよ！
lines.kana: ちょっとみせて。え、これ、おなかのくすりだよ！
lines.english: Let me see. Wait, this is stomach medicine!

lines.speaker: sora
lines.romaji: uso! kenta ga kaze no kusuri da tte itteta noni.
lines.ja: うそ！ケンタが風邪の薬だって言ってたのに。
lines.kana: うそ！けんたがかぜのくすりだっていってたのに。
lines.english: No way! Kenta told me it was cold medicine!

lines.speaker: mai
lines.romaji: onaka no kusuri ja, kikanai yo. kaze no kusuri motte kita kara, kore nonde.
lines.ja: お腹の薬じゃ、効かないよ。風邪の薬持ってきたから、これ飲んで。
lines.kana: おなかのくすりじゃ、きかないよ。かぜのくすりもってきたから、これのんで。
lines.english: Stomach medicine won't do anything for that. I brought some cold medicine, so take this.

lines.speaker: sora
lines.romaji: arigatou. kono kusuri wa kiku no?
lines.ja: ありがとう。この薬は効くの？
lines.kana: ありがとう。このくすりはきくの？
lines.english: Thanks. And does this one actually work?

lines.speaker: mai
lines.romaji: un, yoku kiku yo. watashi, kaze hiitara itsumo kono kusuri da yo.
lines.ja: うん、よく効くよ。私、風邪ひいたらいつもこの薬だよ。
lines.kana: うん、よくきくよ。わたし、かぜひいたらいつもこのくすりだよ。
lines.english: Yeah, it works really well. Whenever I catch a cold, this is what I take.

lines.speaker: sora
lines.romaji: jaa, nomu ne. a, kusuri, mou kiite kita ki ga suru.
lines.ja: じゃあ、飲むね。あ、薬、もう効いてきた気がする。
lines.kana: じゃあ、のむね。あ、くすり、もうきいてきたきがする。
lines.english: Okay, down it goes. Oh, I think it's kicking in already.

lines.speaker: mai
lines.romaji: kusuri, ima nonda bakkari desho. ashita mo netsu ga attara, byouin itte ne.
lines.ja: 薬、今飲んだばっかりでしょ。明日も熱があったら、病院行ってね。
lines.kana: くすり、いまのんだばっかりでしょ。あしたもねつがあったら、びょういんいってね。
lines.english: You only just took it. If you've still got a fever tomorrow, go and see a doctor, OK?

lines.speaker: sora
lines.romaji: ee, byouin, hitori de iku no iya da naa.
lines.ja: えー、病院、一人で行くの嫌だなあ。
lines.kana: えー、びょういん、ひとりでいくのいやだなあ。
lines.english: Ugh, the doctor's? I hate going on my own.

lines.speaker: mai
lines.kana: じゃあ、わたしもいくよ。

lines.speaker: sora
lines.romaji: honto? jaa, ashita mo netsu ga aru to ii naa.
lines.ja: ほんと？じゃあ、明日も熱があるといいなあ。
lines.kana: ほんと？じゃあ、あしたもねつがあるといいなあ。
lines.english: Really? Then I hope I've still got a fever tomorrow.

lines.speaker: mai
lines.romaji: mou, nani itteru no. ii kara, nete.
lines.ja: もう、何言ってるの。いいから、寝て。
lines.kana: もう、なにいってるの。いいから、ねて。
lines.english: Oh, honestly. Just go to sleep.

choices.english: Sora saw a doctor, but the medicine he was given there isn't working, so Mai brings him a different one.
Mai brings Sora the wrong medicine by mistake, so he decides to go to the doctor on his own tomorrow.
Sora has been taking stomach medicine for his cold, so Mai gives him cold medicine and offers to go to the doctor with him.

questions.explanation: Line 4: Sora hasn't been to the doctor (byouin wa ittenai), but he's taking medicine. Line 6: it isn't working at all (zenzen kikanai). Line 7: Mai looks and sees it's stomach medicine (onaka no kusuri), which Kenta had told him was cold medicine (line 8). Line 9: she gives him the cold medicine she brought. Line 13: if he still has a fever tomorrow he should see a doctor, and when he says he hates going on his own (line 14), she says she'll come too (line 15: watashi mo iku yo). A is wrong: Sora hasn't been to the doctor at all (line 4), and the medicine that didn't work came from Kenta. B is wrong: the wrong medicine was Kenta's, and Mai brought the right one. Sora doesn't want to go to the doctor on his own (line 14), so Mai offers to go with him.

questions.english: Kenta (whose stomach medicine Sora was taking) says to you, "kinou kara zutto onaka ga itai n da yo ne. dou shiyou." Tell him to see a doctor, using byouin ni iku.
questions.ja: 昨日からずっとお腹が痛いんだよね。どうしよう。
questions.kana: きのうからずっとおなかがいたいんだよね。どうしよう。
questions.romaji: kinou kara zutto onaka ga itai n da yo ne. dou shiyou.
questions.answer: Tell him to go to the byouin: byouin itta hou ga ii yo (you should see a doctor), or suggest it with byouin ni itte mitara? With a friend, ni usually drops.

modelAnswers.romaji: sore, byouin itta hou ga ii yo.
modelAnswers.ja: それ、病院行った方がいいよ。
modelAnswers.english: You should get that looked at by a doctor.

modelAnswers.romaji: jaa, kyou byouin ni itte mitara?
modelAnswers.ja: じゃあ、今日病院に行ってみたら？
modelAnswers.english: Then why not go and see a doctor today?

questions.explanation: In the scene Mai asks byouin wa? itta? (line 3) and tells Sora byouin itte ne (line 13), and Sora answers byouin wa ittenai (line 4). Byouin is any doctor's clinic, not just a big hospital, so it's the normal word even for a stomachache or a cold. The verb is iku: English 'see a doctor' pulls toward isha o miru or isha ni au, which Japanese doesn't say for a visit. Advice takes -ta hou ga ii, and between friends ni usually drops (byouin itta hou ga ii yo). Kenta is a friend, so answer casually.

questions.english: You've had a headache all afternoon. Mai notices and says, "atama itai no? kusuri aru yo." Answer using kusuri o nomu: ask if you can take some, or say you've already taken some.
questions.kana: あたまいたいの？くすりあるよ。
questions.romaji: atama itai no? kusuri aru yo.
questions.answer: Pair kusuri with nomu: sono kusuri, nonde mo ii? (can I take some of that?) or mou kusuri nonda (I've already taken something). In casual speech o drops.

modelAnswers.romaji: honto? arigatou. jaa, sono kusuri, nonde mo ii?
modelAnswers.ja: ほんと？ありがとう。じゃあ、その薬、飲んでもいい？
modelAnswers.english: Really? Thanks. Can I take some, then?

modelAnswers.romaji: arigatou. demo daijoubu, mou kusuri nonda kara.
modelAnswers.ja: ありがとう。でも大丈夫、もう薬飲んだから。
modelAnswers.english: Thanks, but I'm OK. I've already taken something.

questions.explanation: Medicine takes nomu, the verb for drinking, even when it's a pill: Sora says kusuri nonderu (line 4) and kono kusuri, kinou kara nonderu noni (line 6), and Mai tells him kore nonde (line 9). English 'take' pulls toward toru, but kusuri o toru means picking the medicine up or fetching it, not swallowing it. In casual speech o drops (kusuri nonda). Mai is a friend, so a casual answer fits.

questions.english: Sora tells Mai he's been taking medicine. She asks, "de, kusuri wa kiita?" What is she asking?
questions.ja: マイさんは、何を聞きましたか？
questions.kana: まいさんは、なにをききましたか？
questions.romaji: mai-san wa, nani o kikimashita ka?

choices.english: Whether he asked anyone what the medicine was for.
Whether the medicine has made him feel any better.
Whether he'd heard of that medicine before.

questions.explanation: Line 5: de, kusuri wa kiita? With medicine as the subject, kiku means 'take effect', so Mai is asking whether it has worked. Sora's answer settles it: zenzen kikanai n da yo (line 6), it isn't doing anything. Mai later says stomach medicine won't work (line 9: onaka no kusuri ja, kikanai yo), and Sora asks of the new one, kono kusuri wa kiku no? (line 10). A and C hear the other kiku, 'ask' or 'hear', which sounds exactly the same: Mai uses that one in line 1 (kenta kara kiita yo, Kenta told me), and this question itself uses it (nani o kikimashita ka, what did she ask?). For 'the medicine works', don't reach for hataraku (work at a job): it's kusuri ga kiku, and as it kicks in, kiite kita (line 12).

newWords.english: (not) at all, with a negative (zenzen kikanai: isn't working at all)
have only just done (nonda bakkari: only just took it)
(with a sigh) oh, honestly; come on
